Mentorship & teaching

MS-CC Undergraduate Summer Research Internship

Co-Mentor & Curriculum Developer · Meharry Medical College & Fisk University · Summers 2025 & 2026

I wrote curriculum for and co-mentored the Minority Serving-Cyberinfrastructure Consortium’s 10-week, paid summer research internship, which brings HBCU undergraduates from across the country to Nashville for two weeks of training at Fisk University followed by eight weeks of team research with Meharry. I also led two GIS workshops: mapping social determinants of health and the CDC Social Vulnerability Index for Davidson County, and, in summer 2026, Mapping Cyber Threats.

Recognition & features

Inspiring Black Scientist

Featured, 2026 · Wiley’s Inspiring Black Scientists initiative ↗ · Announcement ↗

Her work focuses on developing data-driven approaches and AI-enabled systems to address complex challenges in public health, critical infrastructure resilience and government operations. Through NWGS Grid™, she brings together wastewater surveillance data, geospatial analytics, genomic information and reference protein structures with curated functional regions to support a broader understanding of infectious-disease surveillance.

1st Place Research Award

2025 · 69th Annual Research Day · School of Applied Computational Sciences, Meharry Medical College

Using GIS and Metagenomics to Enhance Wastewater Surveillance

Clinical surveillance depends on people seeking care and testing, which delays outbreak reporting. This study proposed a framework that pairs campus wastewater sampling with metagenomic analysis in R and spatial mapping in ArcGIS to find pathogen hotspots earlier, with a real-time wastewater surveillance dashboard as the end goal.

Franklin, V.L.; Gary, T.; Sarker, B. (Meharry Medical College); Archer, R. (Tennessee State University). Also presented at the Wastewater Disease Surveillance Summit and the Network of Wastewater-Based Epidemiology, 2025.

Featured by WastewaterSCAN

“She also developed the NWGS Grid Platform, a real-time infectious disease surveillance and analytics system that fuses multiple data sources, wastewater genomic data, clinical results, and contextual population data into a unified ‘smart grid’ that public health teams can use to detect and monitor disease trends as they emerge.”

Kyler Moore, Exploring Wastewater Monitoring Research at HBCUs: A Q&A with a Doctoral Student, WastewaterSCAN ↗, the national wastewater monitoring program led by Stanford University and Emory University.
